option_a.name: NAIRA MATCHING CENTRE · मॅचिंग सेंटर
option_a.positioning: The refined, editorial option. ONE organising idea, kept whole from the base: Naira, which really is a couture house from Nashik, runs the festive season as its own Matching Centre. Every tile is one fabric shade with one real piece matched to it, so the profile itself becomes a twelve-shade card (SHADE N° 01 to N° 12 = posting order). A painted signboard carrying the real wordmark opens the run bottom-right ('MATCHING CENTRE') and closes it top-left ('GUEST ORDERS UNDERTAKEN.'). One ivory shade tag, now fixed in one corner at one size, is the recurring lockup. Four named series carry the guides (THE MATCH, SHADE CARD, माप · THE MEASUREMENTS, THE SAMPLE BLOUSE). The counter is a working service: send the outfit on WhatsApp, get three matches back. It answers the PTAT ask with system (a vernacular institution, a multi-script sign, named series, index carousels, drawn objects around real pieces), while the execution stays in Naira's shipped register: real photography and cut-outs only, flat colour fields with gold hairlines, Velista + Cormorant + Jost with one Devanagari line, one piece per frame, no stickers, and one AI texture in the whole option. WHO SHOULD PICK IT: the owner, if she wants the grid to look like Naira at its best turned up rather than turned into something else; wants every post to sell a match, a set or a gift in time to arrive; and the studio can answer WhatsApp matching requests Mon-Sat 10-7 until 22 Nov.

option_b.name: MANGAL · the Tuesday gold season
option_b.positioning: The maximal, Indian-pop option. ONE organising idea, kept whole from the base: MANGAL. The word means auspicious, and in eight Indian languages it also names Tuesday; it titles the season from Karwa Chauth to the first muhurats. Every tile is a drawn object from Mummy's house (the chalni, the steel almirah, the thali, the faral dabba, the shagun lifafa, the 2006 keypad phone, the school notebook, the shelf of saved boxes, the antarpat) with a real, photographed Naira piece inside it, told as a numbered HOUSE RULE, under one MANGAL seal whose script changes post by post. The spine is the owner's own 10/10 line, 'Not locker gold. Tuesday gold.', and it carries most of her top-scored caption-doc jokes (the dabba, the missed call, the good box). The honesty rule doubles as the look: everything drawn is from Mummy's house, and everything photographed is for sale. It is the closest of the four to the PTAT reference: a multi-script season title, a lockup bracketed by two motifs (coral tulips and the almirah key), real photos inside drawn frames, a steel serving surface as the guide, and series with volumes. It is also the most thumb-stopping grid, on saturated blush, plum, lilac, oxblood and bottle-green grounds with marigold as a printer's second ink. The fixes keep it premium: no sunburst or garlands, no orange grounds, one brand band per tile, no price stack on covers, the densest guide cut, the owner's two approved photo plates left clean, and every script gated by a native reader. WHO SHOULD PICK IT: the owner, if she wants the louder, funnier, more PTAT-like profile built on her own lines; is happy to sign off the added script faces and Kalam inside the drawings; and can line up native readers (Marathi and Hindi at minimum) before posting.

why_these_two: They are the two strongest proposals that are different answers to the owner's brief rather than two versions of one. Matching Centre (245/300) is first overall and is the only proposal that appears in all three judges' recommended pairs. MANGAL (225/300) is second overall and the reference-craft judge's top score (87). Two of the three judges recommended exactly this pair (reference craft outright; brand & truth when the options must differ in kind, as the PTAT ask implies). The organising ideas and the looks are clearly distinct. A is a couture-true Indian institution: a counter of fabric shades, one piece per swatch, quiet flat fields, real photography, service built in. B is an Indian-pop household season: one multi-script word, drawn domestic objects around real pieces, saturated grounds, laugh-out-loud house rules. The other pairings would show the owner one idea twice. Matching Centre + The Fitting Book are both the couture house (pinked swatches, tapes, order slips), which is why the brand judge warned against it. MANGAL + the Reissue are both vernacular nostalgia. The commerce judge preferred the Reissue to MANGAL on build risk and baskets. The fixes answer that: MANGAL's scripts are gated by native readers with a Marathi fallback, its densest guide (the Shaadi Calendar) is cut, its two hardest drawings (the open almirah, the mehndi hands) are simplified, and the BUY line goes from 2 to 7 captions. The Reissue's best Mummy-world piece ('Name: Mummy') is grafted in. The Reissue could not be shown as written: it put 'real gold' in alt text, printed 'waterproof' on 8 tiles including Edition Two pieces, carried no NAIRA wordmark on any cover and invented a FLOWER BRAND sub-brand. The Fitting Book's best pages (the neckline guide, the trial-room reel, real couture swatches, the same-scale tape, cross-references) belong in Matching Centre, and are grafted there without changing its idea.
scoreboard: Judge scores out of 100 (Matching Centre / MANGAL / Reissue / Fitting Book): brand & truth 81 / 69 / 64 / 78; reference craft 84 / 87 / 80 / 72; commerce & build 80 / 69 / 75 / 68. Totals out of 300: Matching Centre 245 (1st), MANGAL 225 (2nd), Reissue 219 (3rd), Fitting Book 218 (4th). Recommended pairs: reference craft = Matching Centre + MANGAL; brand & truth = Matching Centre + MANGAL if the options must differ in kind (Fitting Book only as the 'safest' but same-world B); commerce & build = Matching Centre + Reissue. Matching Centre is in every pair. Why each lost or won: Matching Centre is the truest and most commercial, with only P2 a real claim error; MANGAL has the best wit and the most PTAT-like system, and its weakness was density and build risk, not truth; the Reissue had high per-tile wit but failed on claims hygiene, its invented sub-brand and no wordmark on covers; the Fitting Book was the most useful guides but low on thumb-stop and emblem, too much anatomy to draw, and buried the bestsellers. Must-fix status: every must-fix the three scorecards raised for Matching Centre (P2 piece and claims, P8 'choker', P4 'knots', the Nocturne bracelet's pavé, WhatsApp staffing, P2/P9 grounds, native readers, the fixed tag, the product-free P11, the generic P10 reel, AI textures, re-cutting existing mattes) and for MANGAL (P1 density, ground and product, the P3 tone bracket, native readers, P6 'ruby-red', the seal off clean plates, AI-plate checks, the double mithai, faces, cover density, orange grounds, basket lines, timing honesty, drawing simplification) is resolved in replace_or_fix. None is waived. Grafted posts carry their own judges' must-fixes (the neckline guide on a blouse flat with no anatomy and AI-plate checks; 'Name: Mummy' with a 120 px headline readable in the grid). AI budget for both options together: one generation (A's silk texture) of the eight allowed.
recommendation_to_owner: Post Option A, Naira Matching Centre. It is the only proposal all three judges put in their pair, it finished first overall (245/300), and after the fixes it is the most complete feed. The idea is literally true: a couture house from Nashik matching jewellery the way a matching centre matches a blouse piece, which no competitor can borrow. It gives her the PTAT depth she asked for as a system (a twelve-shade grid, signboard bookends on the diagonal, one tag on nine covers, named series, index carousels, a five-script sign) without leaving the quiet, premium register of her best shipped work. And it sells the season the way the data says it must. The ruby set (₹5,198 at list) sits on the top-left tile that every ad visitor lands on from 22 Nov. The four-gift Sample Blouse goes out on 1 Nov, in time for Diwali delivery, and 'Send this to your brother' eight days before Bhaubeej. A five-function wedding programme and a neckline guide move the 70-unit necklace and the 79-unit Toggle chain. Dhanteras gets the honest voice she scored highest: 'IS IT GOLD? IT'S GOLD TONE.' It is also the safer build: one AI texture, nearly every cut-out already exists, and one Devanagari line per tile. Choose B, MANGAL, if she wants the louder, funnier profile that looks most like the reference and runs on her own lines ('Not locker gold. Tuesday gold.', the dabba, the missed call). It has the stronger thumb-stop and is the bigger swing, and its risk is execution (scripts, faces, drawings), not truth. Settle three things before either is rendered: (1) for A, whether the studio can answer WhatsApp matching requests Mon-Sat 10-7 until 22 Nov; if not, A switches to the site's gifting line and stays strong but loses its service spine, which makes B the closer call; (2) font sign-off: Tiro Devanagari for A; the Tiro family, Noto Serif Gujarati and Malayalam, Gulzar and Kalam (inside drawings only) for B; (3) native readers for every Indic line, with Marathi and Hindi at minimum. Either way, fix three listings: the Bold Nocturne Bracelet's text says 'thick flat curb link' while its photos show a pavé link; the Cushion Halo Ring's alt text says 'adjustable band' while its listing says fixed US 7; and the roster flags the open-back, adjustable Verdant Eternity Band as needs_size.
